finding.claim: Stored SSRF: callbackUrl supplied to subscribe() is saved without validation, and notifyAll() later sends a server-side POST to every stored URL, so an attacker can make the server request arbitrary http/https targets, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of Jobs.subscribe (POST /subscribe body), src/Jobs.java:13
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, with the URI built by URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21

trace.note: callbackUrl stored unvalidated in static subscriptions map, keyed by attacker-controlled name
notifyAll iterates all stored callback values on a per-minute schedule
URI.create(cb) parses the stored string with no scheme, host, or IP allow-list
POST body is the payload; the request is issued by the server
client.send performs the outbound request; response is discarded, so this is at least blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: subscribe(): no validation at all. notifyAll(): no scheme, host, port, or resolved-IP check. HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER, so redirect-based escalation is not in play, but direct requests to private/loopback/link-local addresses are not blocked. Assumption: POST /subscribe is reachable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege user; the auth layer is not in this repo, so this is unverified. A malformed callbackUrl makes URI.create throw IllegalArgumentException, which aborts the loop and stops delivery to all later subscribers (availability issue, not SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe() at src/Jobs.java:13-15 stores callbackUrl with no check. notifyAll() at src/Jobs.java:19-24 calls URI.create(cb) and client.send with no scheme, host, or IP check. The only validation in the file is the regex in thumb() at src/Jobs.java:30, which is on a different code path and does not guard the sink.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: callbackUrl enters subscribe() at Jobs.java:13 (documented as the POST /subscribe body at line 12), is stored unvalidated at line 14, and is POSTed server-side from the loop at lines 19-24 with no closing guard. The one caveat is that the route handler and its auth are not in this repo, so reachability by a low-privilege user is inferred from the comment, not verified, but nothing in the repo indicates the input is admin-only.
